headline: Oil climbed back to about $110 overnight after the US ordered some diplomats and families out of Saudi Arabia following deadly Houthi attacks. Currencies barely moved; the Australian dollar hit a three-week high.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: The dollar index held near 101.6 in Asia trading, close to a three-week low. Oil rose after the US ordered some diplomats out of Saudi Arabia, but that did not reach the dollar overnight. Coming up: weekly US jobless claims at 7:30 AM CT.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: since the US–Iran war began in February, high oil has kept US inflation up, and with it bets that the Federal Reserve raises rates again in December, which supports the dollar. Talk of peace proposals this week pulled the dollar to a three-week low. What changed: overnight the US State Department ordered non-essential staff and families out of its Saudi missions after Houthi attacks killed people at Dammam airport and near Aramco's Shaybah oilfield. The New York Times also reported that the US and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the November 3 midterms; President Trump has not approved them. Oil rose about 1%, but the dollar index stayed near 101.6 and Fed bets did not move: a hold on October 28 is the strong favourite and a December hike about 90% priced. What it means: the dollar is waiting on oil and the war, not on US data. The question to keep asking: does oil stay high enough to keep the Fed's December hike on the table?
chapters.fx: What's next: weekly US jobless claims at 7:30 AM CT (about 200,000 expected) and the US leading index at 9:00 AM CT. Friday: US business surveys (flash PMIs) at 8:45 AM CT and the final University of Michigan sentiment survey at 9:00 AM CT. The Fed stays in its quiet period until its October 28 decision.
numbers: Dollar index ~101.6 (flat; near a three-week low)
Fed: Oct 28 hold ~85%; Dec hike ~90% (CME FedWatch)

scenarios.base: If jobless claims stay near 200,000 and oil holds near $110, the dollar stays close to 101.6.
scenarios.bull: If the Saudi departures widen across the Gulf or strikes on Iran resume, oil and US yields jump and the dollar recovers.
scenarios.bear: If claims rise sharply or a real opening in US–Iran talks drains oil, December hike bets fade and the dollar slips to new monthly lows.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The euro held near $1.123 overnight. France's 10-year borrowing cost sits above 5% ahead of Moody's review of France's credit rating on Friday, and higher oil adds to Europe's energy bill. Coming up: euro-area consumer confidence at 9:00 AM CT.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: the euro has been held back by France's budget fight and by expensive energy, which Europe imports. The European Central Bank is expected to hold on October 29 and lean toward a hike in December, because euro-area inflation is running well above its 2% target. What changed: little in the euro itself overnight; it held near $1.123. Oil's rise after the US pulled some diplomats from Saudi Arabia adds to Europe's import bill, and France's 10-year yield stays above 5%, its highest since 2002, with the gap over Germany the widest since the euro debt crisis. What it means: a likely December ECB hike supports the euro, but France's borrowing costs and energy pull the other way. The question: does Moody's cut France's credit rating on Friday?
chapters.fx: What's next: euro-area consumer confidence at 9:00 AM CT (about −17 expected). Friday: flash business surveys for France (2:15 AM CT), Germany (2:30 AM CT) and the euro area (3:00 AM CT), then Moody's review of France after the close. October 27: the French parliament's revenue vote. October 29: the ECB's decision.
numbers: France 10-year yield above 5% (first since 2002); gap over Germany ~153bp
EUR/GBP ~0.838 (euro near its weakest vs the pound in 17 months)

scenarios.base: If France stays calm until Moody's on Friday, the euro hovers near $1.12.
scenarios.bull: If oil eases or Friday's business surveys come in strong, December hike bets firm and the euro gains.
scenarios.bear: If Moody's cuts France or French yields keep climbing, the euro slips.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: The pound held near $1.34 overnight, close to its strongest against the euro in 17 months. A Bank of England hike on November 5 is all but fully priced after hot UK inflation figures on Wednesday. Coming up: the CBI factory survey at 5:00 AM CT.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: the Gulf war has pushed up energy bills, and Britain, which imports a lot of gas, has felt it more than most. The Bank of England has held rates at 3.75%, but strong jobs figures on Tuesday and UK inflation of 3.5% for September, published Wednesday and above forecasts, made a November hike close to certain. What changed: no new UK news overnight; the pound held its gains near $1.3395. Markets still see a second hike in December as roughly a coin toss. What it means: November is settled, so the pound now moves on whether the Bank will need to go again in December. Higher oil overnight strengthens that case a little, because energy is what is lifting UK prices. The question: how long does the Bank think energy will keep inflation up?
chapters.fx: What's next: the CBI industrial orders survey at 5:00 AM CT (about −20 expected) and UK consumer confidence from GfK at 6:01 PM CT. Friday: UK retail sales for September at 1:00 AM CT and flash business surveys at 3:30 AM CT. October 28: the UK budget. November 5: the Bank of England's decision.
numbers: BoE: Nov 5 hike ~95–99%; Dec second hike ~51%
UK CPI 3.5% y/y in September (3.4% expected)
EUR/GBP ~0.838 (pound's strongest vs the euro in 17 months)

scenarios.base: If the surveys hold steady, the pound stays near $1.34 into Friday's retail sales.
scenarios.bull: If retail sales or business surveys surprise higher, December hike bets rise and so does the pound.
scenarios.bear: If spending figures disappoint, December bets fade and the pound gives back some of its gains.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: The dollar held near ¥158 overnight. Japan's national inflation figures, out at 6:30 PM CT tonight, will shape the case for a Bank of Japan rate hike in December, which markets now see as likely.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: the yen is the weakest major currency on the board, because Japan's rates are far below everyone else's and Japan pays heavily for imported energy. The Bank of Japan is expected to hold on October 30 and is increasingly expected to hike in December. What changed: the dollar stayed in a narrow range near ¥158 in Asia trading. Wider Gulf tensions did not bring the usual rush into the yen, as higher oil hurts Japan's trade bill. Reports that the Bank of Japan may raise its inflation forecast this month keep the December hike case firm, at about 80% priced. What it means: the yen needs a hike, or clear signals of one, to recover. The question: does inflation give the Bank of Japan cover to move in December?
chapters.fx: What's next: Japan's national core inflation for September at 6:30 PM CT tonight (2.1% expected, up from 1.7%), then Japan's flash business surveys at 7:30 PM CT. October 29–30: the Bank of Japan's decision.
numbers: Japan core CPI forecast 2.1% y/y (1.7% in August)

scenarios.base: If Japan's inflation comes in near 2.1%, the dollar stays close to ¥158.
scenarios.bull: If inflation runs hotter or the Bank of Japan hints at October, the yen gains.
scenarios.bear: If inflation comes in soft, December hike bets fade and the yen weakens toward ¥159.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The dollar held near 0.824 francs overnight. The Gulf escalation did not trigger a rush into the franc. Coming up: the Swiss National Bank's summary of its September policy discussion at 2:30 AM CT.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: the Swiss franc is a safe place to park money in a crisis, but Swiss inflation is near zero, so the Swiss National Bank holds rates at 0% and markets see a cut in December as a real chance. What changed: little; the dollar eased slightly to about 0.824 francs. The Saudi departures and reports of post-midterm strike plans on Iran did not bring safe-haven buying, as markets treated them as more of the same. What it means: the franc gains when fear spikes, but low Swiss inflation keeps the central bank leaning toward easier policy, which caps it. The question: does the bank's summary sound more worried about a strong franc?
chapters.fx: What's next: the Swiss National Bank's summary of its September policy discussion at 2:30 AM CT. December 10: its next decision.
numbers: SNB policy rate 0%; next decision Dec 10

scenarios.base: If the summary repeats the bank's known stance, the franc stays near 0.82 per dollar.
scenarios.bull: If the Gulf conflict escalates, safe-haven buying lifts the franc.
scenarios.bear: If the bank stresses its readiness to cut or step into currency markets, the franc softens.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The Australian dollar rose about 0.7% to around 70.3 US cents, a three-week high and the best performer among major currencies. Markets now see roughly even odds of a Reserve Bank of Australia hike on November 3.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Australia's inflation has picked up with energy prices, and the Reserve Bank of Australia has been weighing whether to raise rates again. Earlier this week deputy governor Andrew Hauser said the inflation outlook was materially worse, and Goldman Sachs moved to expect a November hike. What changed: the Australian dollar extended its gains in Asia trading to about 0.703, a three-week high, as bets on a November 3 hike held near 40–55%. Higher prices for the goods Australia sells abroad also help. What it means: the more likely a November hike looks, the more support for the Australian dollar. The question: does Australia's third-quarter inflation report on October 28 settle the November decision?
chapters.fx: What's next: Australia's flash business surveys at 5:00 PM CT today. October 28: third-quarter consumer prices, the key input. November 2–3: the Reserve Bank of Australia's decision.

scenarios.base: If the business surveys hold up, the Australian dollar stays near 70 cents into the inflation report.
scenarios.bull: If the surveys come in strong, November hike bets rise and the Australian dollar extends its gains.
scenarios.bear: If Gulf fear hits stock markets, the Australian dollar, which tends to fall when investors get nervous, gives back its gains.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The US dollar held near 1.404 Canadian dollars overnight. A Bank of Canada hike on October 28 is close to fully priced, and higher oil helps Canada as a big exporter. Coming up: Canadian producer prices at 7:30 AM CT.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: high oil lifts Canada's export income but also its inflation. Last week Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem said the bank's inflation forecast would be revised substantially higher on energy, and markets moved quickly to expect a hike on October 28. What changed: the loonie edged up, with the US dollar near 1.404 Canadian, as oil rose about 1% after the US pulled some diplomats from Saudi Arabia. Hike odds held near 93%. What it means: a hike is mostly in the loonie's price already, so a hold would be the surprise. Higher oil adds a small extra lift. The question: does the bank signal more hikes after October?
chapters.fx: What's next: Canada's producer and raw materials prices and new housing prices at 7:30 AM CT. Friday: Canadian retail sales for August at 7:30 AM CT. October 28: the Bank of Canada's decision.

scenarios.base: If oil holds near $98 and the price data match forecasts, the loonie stays near 1.40 per dollar.
scenarios.bull: If oil climbs further or price data run hot, the case for more Bank of Canada hikes lifts the loonie.
scenarios.bear: If oil falls on a Gulf de-escalation, the loonie loses its energy support.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: New Zealand's inflation slowed to 3.7% in the third quarter, slightly below forecasts. The kiwi dipped to about 56.9 US cents, then recovered toward 57, because markets still see a Reserve Bank of New Zealand hike next week as near certain.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: New Zealand's central bank, the RBNZ, has turned toward raising rates as energy and food push inflation above its 1–3% target band. What changed: consumer prices rose 0.7% in the third quarter, a touch below the 0.8% forecast, and 3.7% over the year, down from 4.1% and just under both forecasts and the bank's own 3.9% projection. That is still above the target band, and core inflation stayed firm. Markets kept the October 28 hike near fully priced, and see two hikes by February as certain. The kiwi dipped to about 0.569 on the release, then recovered to about 0.571. What it means: a slightly soft print did not change the bank's path, so the kiwi's support from higher rates holds. The question: does the RBNZ signal more than one hike when it meets?
chapters.fx: What's next: no major New Zealand data before the RBNZ's decision on October 28. Until then the kiwi moves with risk appetite and the US dollar.
numbers: NZ CPI Q3: 0.7% q/q (0.8% expected); 3.7% y/y (3.8% expected; 4.1% prior)

scenarios.base: If risk appetite holds, the kiwi stays near 57 cents into the RBNZ decision.
scenarios.bull: If the RBNZ signals a run of hikes, the kiwi gains.
scenarios.bear: If Gulf fear spreads to stock markets or the dollar firms, the kiwi slips back toward 56 cents.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Brent crude rose about 1% to roughly $110 a barrel in Asia trading after the US ordered some diplomats' families and staff to leave Saudi Arabia, following deadly Houthi attacks near Saudi oil sites and an airport.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: oil has been high since the US–Iran war began in February, with attacks on Gulf shipping and energy sites keeping a risk premium in prices. On Wednesday Brent briefly topped $110, then faded after the US Treasury let some blacklisted tankers unload. What changed: overnight the US ordered non-essential staff and families out of Saudi Arabia. Houthi strikes killed people at Dammam airport and, via drone debris, near Aramco's Shaybah oilfield. The New York Times reported US and Israeli plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the November 3 midterms, not yet approved by President Trump. Brent rose to about $110.11 and US crude to about $98.12. What it means: the risk of supply damage in Saudi Arabia itself is rising, which keeps oil's premium in place. That feeds inflation worries everywhere and helps oil exporters' currencies like the Canadian dollar. The question: do attacks reach oil output, or stay near-misses?
chapters.fx: What's next: any widening of the US departure order beyond Saudi Arabia, further Houthi strikes on Saudi sites, and US natural gas storage figures at 9:30 AM CT.
numbers: US crude stocks −3.1M barrels last week (EIA)
At least 18 attacks on shipping in two weeks (Kpler, via Reuters)

scenarios.base: If attacks stay away from oil output, Brent hovers near $110.
scenarios.bull: If a strike damages Saudi production or the departures widen across the Gulf, Brent jumps well above $110.
scenarios.bear: If Washington eases more sanctions or talks with Iran restart, Brent slips back toward $105.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold held near $4,115 an ounce overnight after five straight down days. High US rates and a firm Fed hike outlook weigh on it, and new Gulf tension has not brought buyers back.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: gold ran to records this year on war fears and central-bank buying, but it has slipped as US yields climbed toward their highest in years, since gold pays no interest. What changed: gold eased about 0.2% to near $4,115 in Asia trading. The US departure order in Saudi Arabia and reports of post-midterm strike plans on Iran did not spark safe-haven buying. What it means: for now, high US yields matter more for gold than war headlines. Hedge funds are still strongly betting on gold, though they have trimmed. The question: does a real escalation, or falling US yields, break the losing streak?
chapters.fx: What's next: US jobless claims at 7:30 AM CT, which move US yields. Any confirmed strike on Iran or Saudi oil sites would be the clearest trigger for safe-haven buying.
numbers: CFTC Oct 13: hedge funds strongly for gold, trimming

scenarios.bull: If strikes on Iran resume or US yields fall, gold rebounds.
scenarios.bear: If US data keep the December Fed hike firm and yields rise, gold extends its slide.
